quote: And I’ve grasped some solid and useful things in drawing and in painting, more firmly than you think, my dear friend. But I keep on making what I can’t do yet in order to learn to be able to do it.
source: Vincent van Gogh, The Letters, no. 528, to Anthon van Rappard, Nuenen, 18 August 1885 (trans. Van Gogh Museum edition, 2009)

evidence.where: The full English translation of letter 528 on the Van Gogh Museum's scholarly edition site, read in the printable view. The two sentences appear verbatim in section 2v:6, immediately after which isn't exactly the easiest part of the job! The page header confirms the recipient Anthon van Rappard, the place Nuenen, the date on or about Tuesday, 18 August 1885, and the old Complete Letters number R57.
evidence.edition: Vincent van Gogh: The Letters, ed. Leo Jansen, Hans Luijten and Nienke Bakker (Van Gogh Museum and Huygens ING, 2009)
evidence.locator: Letter 528, section 2v:6, in the reply to Van Rappard's charge that the work is extremely weak

reason: The wording is the Van Gogh Museum edition's own, word for word, and not the smoother rendering that usually travels under Picasso's name, so the card prints a sentence that exists on a named scholarly page. The letters themselves were first published long before 2000; the 2009 date belongs to the translation, which the source line names as the rules require. Van Gogh is new to the year and stands at none of three.
